## `Core/Camera/Camera2D.h`

- `class Camera2D` — A 2D game camera, in the manner of Godot's Camera2D and Cinemachine's follow camera: it follows one or more targets with a dead zone, look-ahead and smoothing, zooms to fit several, stays inside limits, and gives the view the world is drawn through.
- `Camera2D`: `explicit Camera2D(const FloatRect& viewport, const CameraSettings& settings = { })` — Throws std::invalid_argument for settings that are not IsValid.
- `Camera2D`: `void SetViewport(const FloatRect& viewport)` — Where on the canvas it draws.
- `Camera2D`: `[[nodiscard]] const FloatRect& Viewport() const`
- `Camera2D`: `void SetSettings(const CameraSettings& settings)` — Throws std::invalid_argument for settings that are not IsValid.
- `Camera2D`: `[[nodiscard]] const CameraSettings& Settings() const`
- `Camera2D`: `void SetLimits(std::optional<FloatRect> limits)`
- `Camera2D`: `void Follow(Float2 target)` — What to keep in view from the next Update on, until changed: a point, or several with weights and radii.
- `Camera2D`: `void Follow(std::span<const CameraTarget> targets)`
- `Camera2D`: `void Follow(std::initializer_list<CameraTarget> targets)`
- `Camera2D`: `void StopFollowing()` — Stays where it is; SetPose moves it by hand.
- `Camera2D`: `[[nodiscard]] std::span<const CameraTarget> Targets() const`
- `Camera2D`: `void Update(float seconds)` — Moves towards the targets: frame seconds in a view (game time, so a hitstop holds it), step.seconds in a simulation.
- `Camera2D`: `void Snap()` — Jumps to where it is heading, with no smoothing or look-ahead left over: a level's start, a teleport, a cut.
- `Camera2D`: `void SetPose(const CameraPose& pose)` — Places it by hand, for a cutscene or a tweened CameraPose; limits still apply.
- `Camera2D`: `[[nodiscard]] const CameraPose& Pose() const`
- `Camera2D`: `[[nodiscard]] CameraView View() const` — What it shows now.
- `Camera2D`: `[[nodiscard]] CameraView View(float alpha) const` — Between the last two updates by 'alpha' (0..1): a camera updated in a simulation's steps, drawn at runner.Alpha().
- `Camera2D`: `[[nodiscard]] FloatRect VisibleArea() const` — The world rectangle it shows, ignoring rotation.
- `Camera2D`: `[[nodiscard]] Float2 ToWorld(Float2 canvas) const` — A canvas point (the mouse) in the world, and back.
- `Camera2D`: `[[nodiscard]] Float2 ToCanvas(Float2 world) const`
- `Camera2D`: `[[nodiscard]] bool Shows(Float2 world, float radius = 0.0f) const`
- `Camera2D`: `[[nodiscard]] Float2 Focus() const` — What the follow is aiming at, for guides and tests: the targets' point with offset and look-ahead, and where the camera is heading after the dead zone, fitting and limits.

## `Core/Camera/CameraSettings.h`

- `struct CameraFollow` — How a camera follows its targets.
- `CameraFollow`: `Float2 deadZone { }` — The box around the middle of the view the targets move in without moving the camera (Godot's drag margins, Cinemachine's dead zone): {0.2, 0.3} is a fifth of the width and three tenths of the height.
- `CameraFollow`: `float smoothTime = 0.15f` — Seconds the camera takes to catch up, slowing down without overshooting; 0 follows at once.
- `CameraFollow`: `Float2 lookAhead { }` — Seconds of the targets' motion to look ahead, per axis: {0.4, 0} for a side-scroller.
- `CameraFollow`: `float lookAheadLimit = 0.25f` — The most look-ahead, as a fraction of the visible area.
- `CameraFollow`: `float lookAheadSmoothTime = 0.4f` — Seconds look-ahead takes to settle, so a turn swings the view over instead of jerking it.
- `CameraFollow`: `Float2 offset { }` — World units added to where the targets are: look a little above a character's feet.
- `struct CameraZoom` — How a camera zooms.
- `CameraZoom`: `float zoom = 1.0f`
- `CameraZoom`: `bool fit = false`
- `CameraZoom`: `float min = 0.5f`
- `CameraZoom`: `float max = 1.0f`
- `CameraZoom`: `float padding = 0.0f`
- `CameraZoom`: `float smoothTime = 0.3f`
- `struct CameraSettings`
- `CameraSettings`: `CameraFollow follow { }`
- `CameraSettings`: `CameraZoom zoom { }`
- `CameraSettings`: `std::optional<FloatRect> limits` — The world the camera may show (Godot's limits, Cinemachine's confiner).
- `CameraSettings`: `bool pixelSnap = false` — Moves the world by whole canvas units only: crisp code-drawn lines on a slowly moving camera.
- `[[nodiscard]] bool IsValid(const CameraSettings& settings)` — False for negative or non-finite values, a dead zone or look-ahead limit above 1, zooms that are not above 0, min above max, or empty limits.

- `CameraView`: `[[nodiscard]] CameraView Parallaxed(float factor) const` — The view of something nearer or farther than the world: 1 is this view, 0 stays on the screen whatever the camera does, and above 1 moves faster than the world, as what is close to the eye does.
- `CameraView`: `[[nodiscard]] constexpr FloatRect VisibleArea() const` — The world rectangle the viewport shows, ignoring rotation; empty without a viewport or zoom.
